definition: The most advanced AI capabilities at the cutting edge of what current systems can achieve, typically associated with the largest models and highest compute budgets.
rationale_for_coinage: Accelerationists treat frontier capability as a competitive advantage and progress marker. Safetyists see frontier capability as the level requiring the most stringent safety evaluation. Skeptics view it as a marketing term obscuring actual performance characteristics. The bare term conceals whether 'frontier' is celebrated, feared, or debunked.

do_not_confuse_with.note: Capabilities scaling describes the growth trajectory; frontier capability describes the current leading edge.
Capabilities hazard frames capability as a source of danger; frontier capability frames it as achievement or marketing.

contested_aspects: Whether frontier capabilities represent genuine progress or hype
Whether frontier status should trigger special regulatory requirements
Whether the framing of 'frontier' privileges large-compute developers
